clue.text: Oarsman in a drowsy state taken aback by maroon

indicators.note: taken aback means the whole assembled run is read backwards
in means the oarsman sits inside the word for the drowsy state

parts.note: kif (or kef) is a dreamy, drowsy state, as induced by cannabis
an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: A drowsy rower is startled by someone being marooned, or by a dark red colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maroon' looks like the colour or a castaway, but a maroon is a warning rocket; 'taken aback' turns the whole assembled run round.
explanation.definitionFit: A maroon is a loud signal rocket, a kind of pyrotechnic.

clue.text: Fellow visits dishonest amusement park

parts.note: unfair means unjust or dishonest

explanation.surface: A man goes to a crooked fairground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visits' is a link here: F simply comes before UNFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair with rides and sideshows is a pleasure ground.

clue.text: Loaded, we go in for encouraging the horse

indicators.note: go in tells us the word we is placed inside the word for loaded

parts.note: rolling (in it) means very rich, loaded

explanation.surface: Rich people bet on horses to spur them on.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowel is the spiked wheel on a spur, so rowelling is spurring a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To rowel is to prick a horse with the spiked wheel of a spur, urging it on.

clue.text: Piers employed in the marrow harvest

indicators.note: employed in means the letters are found at work inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone named Piers helps at the vegetable harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piers' looks like a man's name, but it is the plural of pier.
explanation.definitionFit: Wharves and piers are both landing places for ships.

clue.text: Bring up King? George the second brought up

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means moved to the top, so the second letter of George rises to the front

explanation.surface: A question about King George II being raised to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second' names the second letter of George, E, which 'brought up' moves to the top of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To regorge is to vomit or throw back up.

clue.text: Best man put in a request

indicators.note: put in tells us the word for man is placed inside the word best

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: At a wedding, the best man submits a request.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or earnest request, as in 'at his bidding'.

clue.text: Associate of Procrustes?

parts.note: Procrustes was the Greek robber who forced victims to fit his bed, so anyone lying on it was literally his companion in bed

explanation.surface: A question about who kept company with a figure of Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Procrustes stretched or cut his guests to fit his bed, so a companion of his would be one who shared it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shares a bed, or figuratively an ally or partner.

clue.text: Irreligious chap has a lot of capital

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a chap

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the city's name, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Athens is the capital of Greece

explanation.surface: A man with no religion has plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan or ungodly person has no faith in the accepted religion.

clue.text: Have doubts about the weight

definitions.meaning: to hesitate on grounds of conscience
an old apothecaries' unit equal to twenty grains

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hesitate from conscience; as a noun, an apothecaries' unit of twenty grains.

clue.text: Sadly England contains few who are original and trendy

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters are in a sorry, disordered state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament that England has few people who are original and fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' tempts you to put one piece inside another, but it is only a link: both words go into the anagram together.
explanation.definitionFit: Newfangled things are novel and modish, often with a hint of disapproval.

clue.text: Battlefield

parts.note: read as 'battle' plus 'field': a city in Israel famous for crusader sieges, and also a unit of field area

explanation.walkthrough: The port in Israel was besieged in the Crusades; the same word is a measure of land, roughly the size of a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The port city was the site of the great crusader siege of 1189-91, and the word is also a measure of farmland.

clue.text: Typically, RMA is in disarray…

parts.note: RMA is the word arm with its letters jumbled, so it is a typical example of letters scattered everywhere

explanation.surface: A remark that the Royal Military Academy is, as usual, in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: RMA looks like the Royal Military Academy, but it is simply ARM with its letters jumbled, an example of something in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things scattered everywhere in a disorderly way.

clue.text: …put out again by soldier and his cockney girl

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords

indicators.note: cockney speech drops the initial H, so his becomes 'is

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, a soldier and his London girlfriend are thrown out again.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney (East Londoner) drops the H from his, leaving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue is to publish or release once more.

clue.text: Still wanting retribution, man at first 'overed round church centre

annotationWithheld.why: Still wanting retribution, man at first 'overed round church centre (9): 'UNG (hovered, cockney) round NAVE plus ED gives the answer, but 'man at first' cannot be reconciled with ED coming last
annotationWithheld.clue: Still wanting retribution, man at first 'overed round church centre

clue.text: Seeing less spectacular play

definitions.meaning: more sightless, comparative of an adjective meaning unable to see
an outstanding performance in sport, as in 'he played a real stormer'

explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of the adjective for sightless; also British slang for a brilliant performance in a game.

clue.text: Bomb — 20, possibly — concealed by leaders of desperate terrorists

indicators.note: concealed by means the anagram is hidden between the first letters of the two words
leaders of means take the first letter of each of the following words
possibly signals that the letters of the referenced answer may be rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 20 down, meaning get back in

explanation.surface: Desperate terrorists hide a bomb that might enter again.
explanation.walkthrough: '20' points to 20-down; 'possibly' rearranges its letters into ETERREN, which sits between D and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear bomb is held as a weapon to discourage attack.

clue.text: Note the horse — he attracts notice, being endowed with brains

parts.note: E is a musical note
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse
taken as written
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A clever horse with a note attached draws attention to itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attracts' and 'being endowed with' are links; 'brains' is used in its informal sense of a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a 'brains' is a clever person, an intellectual or highbrow.

clue.text: Detective sticks to weed

parts.note: gums means sticks with glue
to hoe is to weed

explanation.surface: A private eye sticks to gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a private investigator.

clue.text: What's often buried and, abroad, kept under cover

indicators.note: kept under means the second part is placed below the first in this down clue

parts.note: a hatch is a cover over an opening
et is French, a language abroad, for and

explanation.surface: Something commonly buried and, overseas, hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'bury the hatchet' is to make peace. ET, French for 'and', goes under HATCH in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'bury the hatchet' means to make peace, so this axe is what's put underground.

clue.text: More unpleasantly warm, I removed jumper

indicators.note: removed tells us the letter I is taken out of the comparative

parts.note: sweatier means hotter and more uncomfortable

explanation.surface: Feeling too hot, I took off my pullover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a pullover, not a person who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumper is the British word for a knitted pullover.

clue.text: Do diamonds follow you and me about noisily?

indicators.note: follow means the diamonds come after the preceding pieces
about means the word for you and me is turned around

parts.note: us means you and me
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loudly
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A question whether jewels trail after a couple, making a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a verb meaning be enough, as in 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enough or adequate, as in 'that will do'.

clue.text: What's wearing out deer? Not being culled

indicators.note: being culled means the deer herd is broken up, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what wears out deer, followed by the reply that they are not being culled.
explanation.definitionFit: An erodent is an agent that eats away or corrodes.

clue.text: Tenant carries key to get back in

indicators.note: carries means the word for tenant holds the key inside it

parts.note: a renter is a tenant
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A tenant has a key to get back into the flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter again is to go back inside.

clue.text: Former outcaste rehabilitated — that's routine

indicators.note: rehabilitated means restored and remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A former outcast has been reintegrated into society, which is nothing unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done as a natural, expected step is ordinary and habitual.

clue.text: King Henry has turned round

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the letter for Henry
turned means the word has is read backwards

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A king called Henry has turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the monarch of Iran.

clue.text: Waste, eg debris, to get recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction that rubbish such as debris should be sent for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' looks like rubbish, but it is a wasteland: a desert in Mongolia and China.
explanation.definitionFit: A waste is a barren, empty stretch of land, and this is a vast Asian desert.

clue.text: Five write a little

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tad is a small amount

explanation.surface: An instruction to write just five words or so.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentad is a group or set of five.

clue.text: He's willing to try getting a rise

parts.note: to test is to try
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: Someone happy to try anything to get a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's willing' seems to mean eager, but it means he is making a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes a will is, in a pun, one who is willing.
